- I find:
  - The change. It is exactly the seven write-set paths. No line is removed. writer.py gains only module-docstring lines and one block after held_leases, with no import added.
  - session_lease's order (AC1, AC2). The checks run in AC1 and AC2's order:
    - "argument", in its own try;
    - "root", in its own try;
    - the presence step by lstat kind bits: "no_store", "unreadable" or "link";
    - the link check, which compares the normcase of the realpath of the store path with the normcase of the root's realpath joined with the three names. A raise gives "link", and a mismatch gives "link";
    - the URI, made from the checked realpath. A UNC or non-UTF-8 path raises, which gives "unreadable";
    - the connect, by mode=ro, uri=True, the timeout and isolation_level None, then a deferred BEGIN;
    - _check_schema's ValueError, which gives "tables". Any other failure gives "unreadable";
    - then, with no session id: no lease row gives "done"/"no_lease_row", and any lease row gives "lease_row_without_session";
    - with a session id: no lease row gives "no_lease_row", then "session", then "ended" (`is not None`, so "" counts as ended). Only that session's rows are parsed, and a malformed time gives "unreadable". Exactly one row with `expires_at > now` gives "tied"; anything else gives "leases".
  - Handlers and cleanup (AC1, AC3).
    - ROLLBACK runs in an inner finally and close in an outer finally. The connection name is None before the try.
    - Every handler returns a value, and a finding names only the exception's type.
    - The text check confirms no PRAGMA, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or makedirs in the lookup's block.
  - judge (AC4, AC5).
    - It checks now first. Then a present non-str value or a relative root gives "argument". Then come "root_without_session" and "session_without_root".
    - With both values present, it looks up at the given root only, with no search.
    - With neither, it checks the working folder ("argument"), then searches upward from abspath with lstat kind bits: missing entries are passed over, a regular file stops the search, and anything else gives "search". It then looks up the store found with no session id.
    - _map gives "tied" only for done/tied with a lease, and "enforce_nothing" only for done/no_lease_row when the search was made. Every "refused" is passed through, and every other shape gives "entry". An outer except Exception gives "entry" with the type name.
    - So no path I found gives "tied" or "enforce_nothing" wrongly from a real lookup.
  - Imports and calls (AC6). claude_code_store imports only os and writer. Of writer it calls only store_path and session_lease, and it names StoreResult. It has no file, process, clock, environment, input, print or network use, and no string naming the project-state directory.
  - The tests. By my own count there are 47 new test functions: 19 in test_writer.py, 6 in test_writer_files.py, 1 in test_writer_properties.py, 19 in test_claude_code_store.py and 2 in test_claude_code_store_properties.py. This equals evidence66's 47. Each test's docstring names "TASK-066 ACn", and no other task's AC appears in qualified form. They meet AC9's listed cases, except the points carried below.
  - Points of my own:
    - (i) R3-1, confirmed by my own reading. In test_case_and_separator_differences_are_not_links (diff :1262-1265), realpath is called only on store_path(self.root) and self.root (diff :358-360), so the key `short` is never looked up. The real call that follows, with root "root/.", covers only the lexical ".", not an 8.3 name. AC9's short-name case is therefore not exercised as written, and it is not counted as covered.
    - (ii) test_judge_searches_real_folders makes a nested folder with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=outer) (diff :504). I read AC8's "no test creates a link or a folder" as not covering tempfile, which AC8's last clause names as the source of paths in the writer test files. The CI deterministic_rule step reported success. This is a reading, stated.
    - (iii) This point is my inference about Python on Windows; it is unmeasured. realpath may return a UNC form for a project on a mapped network or substituted drive. _store_uri then refuses, so every lookup there gives "unreadable". That is fail-closed, and it falls within the contract's UNC limit, but that limit reaches paths that were not given as UNC.
- Carried limits:
  - Measurement and placement. C6 and P-LOC stay unmeasured. No hook is placed, no matcher chosen, no setting changed and nothing measured (CC-3, the owner's). Claude Code's own hook timeouts are unmeasured.
  - The lexical search (R4-3, R5-1), fail-open. The search climbs lexical parents from abspath. A working folder reached through a link from outside the project's tree finds no store and gives "enforce_nothing". Under DEF-0085, this gates any contract that lets a hook call act on judge's "enforce_nothing".
  - The contract's stated limits:
    - a hook call during a long commit is refused without a record;
    - UNC and non-UTF-8 paths are refused;
    - real links and junctions are never exercised in CI on Linux;
    - links that realpath does not resolve, hard links and bind mounts are not seen;
    - the check and the open are two steps, and a change between them is not seen;
    - a store created, removed or swapped between search and open is a race;
    - an inner store is judged alone;
    - a hook call outside every project's folder tree is not judged;
    - the four-table form is refused until K1;
    - now must come from the process clock (fail-open if it is earlier than the real time).
  - WAL (R2-1, R4-5). No WAL-mode store is tested. Whether a read-only open reads one, or creates its side files, is untested. "Creates nothing" is shown only for the rollback-journal form.
  - The docstring breadth (R4-1, R4-2). A raise while checking now gives "argument: now (<type>)", not "entry". Reading R-d has the same breadth.
  - Two checks of now (R4-4). judge's MRO-name check and the writer's isinstance check differ. Both fail closed, and the difference is stated only in reading R-a.
  - The _map guard (R5-2). done/tied is accepted on the search path, which the real lookup cannot produce.
  - Untested points:
    - R3-1, the short-name case, also my point (i);
    - R3-2, J9, which is caught only by the unit module;
    - R3-3, R4-6 and R5-3, M9 (the deferred BEGIN), which is caught only by a source-text check. The IMMEDIATE-lock test's docstring is not proof of the deferred lock.
  - Broken copies (R3-4). They were run against the scratchpad code copy. After the first run only 16 mutations were rerun (D-1372, D-1373; not reopened). The 35-of-35 result is the implementer's claim. The equality of the archived now/ files and diff with the head is now machine output (D-1379 (c), 7 of 7 and the diff equal), but the values are worker-supplied.
  - R3-5. The names check covers only class methods named test*. The diff has no top-level test function.
  - CI (R1-1, R3-6, R4-7). ci-read names the base commit. The run's headSha 3998a378… and its 21 successful steps are read from ci-job-t66a.txt.
  - The patches (R1-2). The presence and link stand-ins patch functions of the global os module for one call each. This is safe in a single-threaded suite. It is a limit only.
  - Unrun checks (R2-2, R5-4, R1-3). Bandit was not run locally; CI ran it. The reviewers ran nothing.
  - The implementer's claims. The local runs (unit 1315, integration 136 with one skip, property 165), deterministic_rule (182 files, 0 findings), the pre-scans and the AC6 and AC8 acceptance-time scripts are all claims. The AC6 and AC8 scripts are judged at acceptance.
  - My points (ii) and (iii) above.
  - The departure (D-1376 C1). The five review prompts were not compared with their briefs at launch. The later comparison (D-1378 C2) shows each prompt, as sent and as received, equal to its brief file but for the file's one trailing LF.
  - Deferred items. DEF-0076, DEF-0077, DEF-0078 and DEF-0080 to DEF-0084 stay as they are. DEF-0085 holds the text and test points above.

basis:
DA-3: ai_review (cross-model), the decision agent's half of the pair, decision agent (claude-opus-5-5, definition 3dd46b53…1219, revision 12), for TASK-066 at commit 3998a378e91fbd08db59f9ef7e7f88ff7b21df89. The way-2 half is R5 at 3998a378 (claude-sonnet-5-5, review66a-R5.txt).
- Fail-closed, by my own reading of claude_code_store.py :110-157 and writer.py :528-670.
  - "tied" comes only from _map :114-115. That needs a writer.StoreResult that is "done" with reason "tied" and a value, which session_lease gives only at writer.py :573. Before that point, every check must pass:
    - the arguments, then the root;
    - lstat kind regular;
    - the normcase(realpath) link check;
    - the URI from the checked realpath;
    - the read-only connect and a deferred BEGIN;
    - _check_schema;
    - a lease row present;
    - the session row present with ended_at NULL;
    - exactly one of that session's leases with expires_at > now.
  - "enforce_nothing" comes only from :147 (no store found) and :117 (done/no_lease_row with searched True, passed only by :148). Both are reachable only after :135-140 have returned for every case with a session id or a root present.
  - With no session id, session_lease returns "lease_row_without_session" for any lease row (writer.py :558-560), so a store holding any row, expired or not, refuses.
  - No exception escapes. judge :154-157 is the outer net; the inner nets are :126 and writer.py :644, :648, :664 and :669. A finding holds fixed words and a type name only.
  - No input or store state I found gives "tied" or "enforce_nothing" where the contract says refuse. The one fail-open case is the stated lexical-search limit (R4-3, R5-1, DEF-0085).
- Imports and effects.
  - claude_code_store imports exactly os and writer (diff :60, :62), and writer.py adds no import.
  - The module opens no file. It only examines the file system: os.lstat of writer.store_path in _probe, os.path.abspath, dirname, isabs and isdir.
  - It has no process, clock, environment, standard input, print, network or model use, and keeps no state.
  - The lookup writes nothing: a mode=ro URI, one deferred transaction ended by ROLLBACK in a finally, close in an outer finally (writer.py :576-589).
- Architecture fit.
  - The three outcomes are spec 5 §11 point 7's bullets 3, 5 and 6 (spec-05 :109-112).
  - The hook side reaches the store only through the writer module's read-only lookup (spec-05 :109; INV-004). The event log is not touched.
  - The search and its pass-over follow spec-05 :110. The inner-store, outside-the-tree and removed-store cases are the spec's stated limits (:111).
  - judge is not wired to any hook (module docstring :47-51). The source of the session id, the root, the working folder and now is a later contract's.
- Points of my own:
  - (i) Passing over a non-folder. A regular file named .aieos in a folder gives FileNotFoundError or NotADirectoryError in _probe (:88), so the folder is passed over. This is within spec-05 :110 ("passing over a folder whose .aieos/ holds no store file") and :111's stated limit that a removed or replaced store turns the hook off with no session id set. It is a stated limit, not a new gap.
  - (ii) R-a. _is_now's check by class name and module (:76-81) would also pass a foreign class that carries those names. On every path that reaches session_lease, writer._check_time's isinstance check (writer.py :134) refuses such a value ("argument", passed through as "refuse"). On the one path that does not reach it, :147 (no store found), now decides nothing. So the difference between the two checks (R4-4) fails closed wherever now matters. I agree with R5 that R-a is a fair reading of AC6.
  - (iii) R-g, M9. On the implementer's run, the IMMEDIATE-lock integration test still gave "tied" under M9 (brka-parts.txt :60, [1, 0, 0]; worker-supplied). So on that SQLite build, BEGIN IMMEDIATE under mode=ro took no lock that a test could see, and the deferred BEGIN is not behaviourally distinguishable there. I agree with R5: the R14 text check is a fair test of AC3's wording "runs a deferred BEGIN", is brittle, and is not a behavioural test. Another SQLite build may refuse BEGIN IMMEDIATE on a read-only connection, which would give "unreadable" (fail closed). That is my inference and unmeasured. The point is carried (DEF-0085, M9).
- R5's points. R5-1 (lexical search, fail-open), R5-2 (the _map guard), R5-3 (M9 by text only) and R5-4 (read only, nothing run) are agreed and carried in DA-1 and DEF-0085. R5's eight traced faults agree with my reading of the deciding lines.
- Limits. The limits listed in DA-1 apply here unchanged. The test, CI, broken-copy and head-equality results are worker-supplied.
- Outcome: pass.
